text: Midway through this project, the source system renames a column with no warning. raw_orders dot status becomes order_status — same data, same meaning, different name, and dbt finds out the hard way.
The very next dbt build fails at the staging model, exactly one layer from the raw source, with an invalid identifier error Snowflake surfaces directly through dbt's build log.

Before touching any SQL, the real first move is dbt ls dash dash select, the staging model, plus. That one command lists exactly which models are affected downstream, using the same ref and source graph the lineage view shows later.

The fix renames only the source-side read inside the staging model, keeping its output column named status. That one deliberate choice contains the blast radius at exactly one file — every downstream model, test, and dashboard keeps working unmodified.

If the rename had propagated past staging, it would have rippled into every downstream model, test, and the Power BI report for a change that carries zero new information. Next: Chapter 4 makes a change like this catchable automatically, through tests and documentation.
